summary: This photo essay from Local Arts and Culture (October 14, 2023) shows how art education in local public schools is being sustained through advocacy and community partnerships despite budget cuts. It moves through images of classrooms, community murals, policymaker exhibits, digital art, cross-curricular work, inclusion, fundraising, self-portraits and educators. The essay argues that art is an indispensable part of education, not an elective.
one_line: A photo essay showing how advocacy, partnerships and teachers sustain art education in local schools amid budget pressures, across many settings.
key_facts: The essay is published by Local Arts and Culture on October 14, 2023, and says schools face budget cuts and shifting priorities.
On September 9, 2023, Mrs. Jennifer Atkins, an art teacher at Thompson Elementary, turned her classroom into a dynamic art studio using paint, clay, and recycled materials.
On September 26, 2023, students from Central High School worked with local artist Miguel Herrera on a community mural representing the neighborhood's cultural heritage.

On the first Tuesday of October, state policymakers were invited to an exhibit of student work at the City Hall Art Space, where a student discussed her environmental-themed artwork with a local council member.
On October 19, 2023, a high school classroom photo shows students using tablets to create digital illustrations.
A September 15, 2023 workshop had math and art teachers guiding students in an art project on geometric concepts, patterns, and symmetry.
On October 5, 2023, Miss Laura Martin, a special education art teacher, led a session where students with various learning disabilities created art alongside their peers.
A September 23, 2023 high school bake sale with posters reading "Supporting Art Education!" raised support for art programs.
Advocates including students presented the case for sustained art funding to the school board at a budget meeting.
On September 30, 2023, students from various grade levels presented self-portraits made through painting, sculpture, and mixed-media.
Mr. David Thompson gave an art history lecture and Ms. Sarah Lim gave one-on-one pottery throwing instruction, as featured among the educators.
The essay concludes that art equips students with cultural literacy and expressive tools crucial for future success.
